question: Should OpenClaw officially publish a best-effort standalone riscv64 image built with experimental Node.js binaries outside the default image attestation contract?
rationale: Source review can assess the implementation, but only release owners can accept the long-term support, supply-chain provenance, registry, and vulnerability-response obligations created under the official image namespace.

options.title: Approve after provenance hardening
options.body: Accept the standalone experimental tag after pinning and authenticating its runtime inputs and completing a protected end-to-end release proof.

options.title: Accept the experimental boundary
options.body: Publish the current best-effort tag while explicitly accepting the unofficial Node and separate-attestation risks as an owned release exception.

options.title: Keep it community-maintained
options.body: Close the official publication path and document the existing community image until an officially supported Node or stronger upstream provenance becomes available.

recommendation.title: Approve after provenance hardening
recommendation.body: Accept the standalone experimental tag after pinning and authenticating its runtime inputs and completing a protected end-to-end release proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history ties this person most directly to Docker release operation, attestation, and runtime-image validation.
